Review Text: The reservation and check in process was a bit sketchy, but it is worth the hassle. We opted for the 30-minute North Biscayne tour.  After figuring out the parking situation, we waited in what appeared to be hotel lobby. Our flight time came and went, we were nervous. Then the tour guide arrived. He apologized for the wait. He led us out to the marina and asked us to sit in a waiting area for a few minutes while he shuttled a couple ahead of us. Upon his return, he led us to a mid-sized boat and ferried us out to the middle of the bay. It was really cool to see the seaplane come in for a landing and then meet up with the boat in the middle of the bay. The boat ride in the bay was added value. The people in the plane jumped in the boat and then we loaded into the plane. It was a Cessna 172 Skyhawk Seaplane. A little older but very well maintained. Our pilot was friendly and very professional. He explained everything he was doing and all the safety features. Our take off was exciting. Our flight was at the end of the day, and we were able to see an absolutely amazing sunset behind the Miami skyline. We flew over the Biscayne National Park. Our pilot narrated the trip the whole way. We flew over the big cruise ships as we approached our landing. The pilot landed the plane in the middle of the bay with a perfect landing. We then met our boat and ferried back to the marina. Our experience was fun, exciting, and well worth the price. The team was very professional. My wife and I felt very safe with the whole flight operation.  If anyone else decides to book with this company, do not worry about the check in process, it will be ok. Hang in there, it is worth it. We met the owner during this tour. He is wonderful person. This is a small company that provides a great experience.  We highly recommend this trip.

Review Text:
I took a chartered flight on Miami Seaplane Tours to Kamalame Cay in the Bahamas with my family, including my infant. Miami Seaplane Tour's operation was unsafe and unprofessional and put me and my family in danger.

The transfer to Kamalame Cay was -- and still is -- advertised on their website. The Sales team promised to “be in touch with the resort about bringing you and picking you up.”

It became clear upon nearing the hotel that this operator is not familiar with transferring hotel guests to Kamalame Cay and has never been in touch with the hotel. The pilot circled and seemed unsure of where to land. He did not fly with a radio so could not contact the hotel. He ultimately decided to touch down in a shallow area where planes are not meant to land. The situation was unsafe and the plane became beached. The hotel staff and my spouse had to get in the water and tow the plan to a safe, deeper water where a boat could pick us up (while my baby cried).

Naturally, I contacted Miami Seaplane Tours to cancel our return flight and request a partial refund. They refused to issue the refund. In fact, they wouldn't even acknowledge the circumstances and sent bizarre emails in response to my requests ("Glad to hear from you Lauren! 😃 We'll see you at 14:00 tomorrow. Weather is supposed to be outstanding. ☀️").

This operator falsely advertised a service and put our family at risk.

One note worth throwing in.... This excursion was literally the last thing we were doing before heading to the airport to catch our flights home, so we arrived at our "meeting spot" (random parking lot near the water), via an UBER with our luggage in hand. Review Text:
My wife, daughter and I were on our way to Andros Island in the Bahamas and we thought booking a charter through Miami Seaplane to get us there might be a neat experience. It was fantastic!

Nicolle was amazing as she helped us with our reservation details. She was very patient with my endless list of questions and she always responded to my inquiries right away. She helped us with a few luggage issues and worked hard to accommodate all of our needs.

Tony was our pilot. What a great guy! He's also a great pilot. I've been on many float planes before, but I've never seen a pilot land one as smoothly as Tony did on this trip. His ability to thread the (cloud) needle was also very impressive. He helped us successfully navigate the Customs/Immigration office in Bimini and he even waited in the Customs office for us so that we could grab a quick bite to eat while the officers arrived.

The flight was indescribably beautiful. The Caribbean Sea is gorgeous from the shore in my opinion, but the view from 2000 feet was more than breathtaking. Tony made sure to point out all the landmarks we passed on the way as well as letting us know when we were about to pass over a ray or shark on the flats. The flight has forever left my family with many great memories.

Unfortunately when it was time for us to return Tropical Storm Emily showed up and we had to, for safety reasons, make other arrangements to get home. One would expect the folks at Miami Seaplane Tours to simply say "see ya next time" but that is not what happened. Nicolle kept me updated on the situation hourly. It worked best for me to make arrangements for my wife and daughter to fly home via New York so they could avoid the storm. I needed to get to Miami to collect some of our luggage (We were in North Carolina the week before our trip to Andros and we had more "stuff" packed than we could safely take on the Seaplane) so I flew to Miami via Atlanta just as the storm subsided. Miami was a bit of a mess after the storm. In some parts of the city people were actually kayaking instead of driving. Despite this Tony went and collected our bags from the storage area and delivered them to me personally. That was over and above the call of duty in my opinion, but the Miami Seaplane Tours folks take their customer service seriously!

My wife and I are small business owners and it's always fun for us to see how other people run their small businesses. Some (more than a few to be honest) small businesses have lousy service and terrible people working for them. Miami Seaplane Tours is just the opposite..................their customers receive great service from simply wonderful people.

I can't wait to fly with them again!

Review Title: One of a Kind SoFlo experience!
Review Text:
My 11 year old son and myself rode in the Cessna 172 pictured on this page. We booked a 1 hour "Ultimate Tour" and had picture perfect weather. Initially, I was a little concerned because the location on Rickenbacker Causeway seemed like a backup or satellite location (Better signage would help), and when no one was there 15 minutes after our appt timed, I called. No sooner than this, Capt Adrian appeared with the plane.

Once on shore, he immediately apologized and took ownership, stating the cause of the delay (Honesty and responsibility? +10 points!) We then loaded quickly, had a quick safety review, then the engine started. We started gliding across the water, and quicker than I thought, we were airborne!

We were airborne in no time and headed out over the main beach. For anyone not used to low level flying, prepare to be amazed and what you can see, and the overall experience! Amazing detail, and you experience Miami and the earth in a whole new way. Being overhead also gives a new dimension to the water, which you can now see through to the bottom in most places.

But nowhere is this better than flying over Biscayne National Park, which is entirely underwater. Our pilot/instructor Adrian narrated the entire flight, explaining sites, significance, history, and even one illegal lobster trap!

The water here spans the full pallet of blue to green, with an emphasis on unbelievable glowing light blue that my camera sadly couldn't duplicate. Depths of water here ranged from 10" to 8 feet, and you can easily spot lots of rays and sharks, especially when we dipped low, and slowed a bit.

Yes, this is a bit more expensive, but any type of aviation is not cheap. But the dividends are well worth it, and formed memories for my son that will last a lifetime!

Great Job Miami Seaplanes! We will be back!

Review Title: Miami Seaplane is the way to go!
Review Text: To celebrate my 30th birthday, my girlfriend and I decided to head out to Bimini just for a quick getaway and taking a seaplane was by far the best choice we made. Our departure time was at noon and our pilot Tony had us in the air at exactly noon.  Even before the flight, Tony offered to take pictures of my girlfriend and I next to the plane just so we can have for memories which I thought was pretty cool.  The flight was actually smooth.  Honestly I was expecting a bumpy ride since it’s a small plane but it wasn’t.  During the flight we were taking pictures of ourselves with the ocean in the background. My girlfriend was ecstatic.  As we got closer to Bimini you could see the ocean color change to a light blue/greenish color.  It was really nice and making the seaplane trip even that much better.  When we got to Bimini, Tony flew us around the Island to point out different restaurants and local places that we could go to.  We even spotted sharks in the water so Tony brought the plane closer to the water so we could take videos and pictures.  The only thing that wasn’t pleasant was once we landed in Bimini we had to wait for Immigration and Customs officers to show up.  Even though Tony called them ahead of time and flew over their office to let them know that we’re about to land, they still took over a half hour to show up.  No fault of Tony’s of course.  After we cleared both Customs and Immigration, Tony called a local cab driver to pick us up and take us to the Hotel.  On the day of departures, again Tony was on time and ready to go but of course, we had to wait for Immigration and Customs again since they have to clear the plane coming from the U.S. and Tony as well.  But once in the air, we were back in Miami in no time.  I’m glad that we chose Miami Seaplane Tours as our transportation to Bimini.  It just made the trip that more special and something that I highly recommend to anyone.  IF YOU’RE GOING TO BIMINI, TAKE MIAMI SEAPLANE TOURS!!!!

Review Title: My husband couldn't have been more pleased!
Review Text:
I took my husband on the "Ultimate Miami and Beaches Seaplane Tour" as a surprise for his 45th birthday, and boy did this gift deliver! I set up our reservation via the phone. Armando was friendly and helpful, delivering customer service throughout the experience that was top notch (in a city just aching for good customer service). The promised confirmation emails arrived promptly and provided clear information and instructions. And when we arrived for our tour a week later, we were greeted by a very nice and experienced pilot, Adriel Anderson, who is a Miami native and clearly passionate about flying. At the start of our tour, he put safety first, giving us a valued briefing on what to do in case of emergency, and then he proceeded to give us an hour of adventure in his comfortable and clean Cessna 172. My husband sat in front next to Adriel, and I sat in back with so much room to look in both directions. My favorite parts of the Tour were seeing the marine life in the water below (Manta, Tarpons, birds, etc.) and touring Stiltsville in Biscayne National Park. So, so beautiful. And the weather was superb. Couldn't have asked for better! My husband says he'll never forget. Thank you, Miami Seaplane Tours!

Tips:

- Pick one of the morning flights if you can. It tends to rain here in the afternoons.

- Don't arrive to your tour early. Five minutes before is sufficient. They don't staff the office since they fly on a reservation basis, and the parking lot isn't right in front of the business, so you can get very hot standing in the sun (not to mention mosquito-bitten).

- Wear light clothes (it can get warm in the plane's cabin) and shoes that you don't mind getting wet.

- Bring a camera.

Review Title: A great way to get to Bimini and small islands
Review Text:
We found by accident that Miami Seaplanes is the best way to fly to Bimini, particularly couples or a family for with typical 'beach trip' luggage. See: www.MiamiSeaplanes.com You can fly into the Miami airport on any airline, and book a flight with Miami Seaplanes to / from Bimini or other small islands and resorts. The transfer to/ from Miami airport is easy -- less time than we spent, by far, in the overcrowded Ft. Lauderdale airport.

We stumbled on this option when my wife was called back for a Board of Directors meeting, in the middle of our vacation. She found Miami Seaplanes on the web, and loved it. The pilot, a great guy, also took our son and his friend up for a short flight around Bimini -- a real adventure.

The seaplane lands on Bimini in the small inlet between the North and South islands, and pulls up on the sand on the North island, down the street from the ferries. You step off onto the beach -- no terminal and no lines! A Bimini Customs official will meet you there.

The other option is United, which now offers once-a-day scheduled flights to Bimini from Ft. Lauderdale airport, with twin-engine Saab turboprops via an alliance with Silver Airlines -- a Carribbean charter service. If you have a larger group or a bunch of luggage, e.g. for scuba or underwater photography, this is the way to go. The dual engine Saab turboprops were very comfortable, like a commuter flight.

The Ft. Lauderdale airport is an overcrowded mess, however, and we were there in February during the 'low' season. I can't imagine what it must be like during Spring Break or the high season.

How to get around when you are there: the place that Miami Seaplanes lands is a short walk from the dock where the little ferries will take you across to South Island, if you are staying at Bimini Sands. If you take the United flight, you will arrive at Bimini's small airport on the South island. A minibus shuttle meets every United flight and will take you to Bimini Sands, or the ferry dock to the North Island -- a 3 to 5 minute drive. Two small ferry boats run back and forth across the shallow inlet between the South and North island -- another 5 minute trip. One ferry is free for residents, but a tip of $2 per visitor is a good idea. The other is run by a local guy, and he charged $2 per person.

You do not need to make a reservation -- the ferries run back and forth all day, from the early
morning into the night. A couple of vendors rent golf carts to get around on the North and South
islands, but we simply walked from the Miami Seaplane beach to the ferry, and from there to Bimini Sands. You could also walk to / from the seaplane to the Big Game Club. Bimini is a very
small place! Taxis are also available, if needed.

In summary, we will definitely book a flight with Miami Seaplanes for our next trip to Bimini. It is quite an experience, and more convenient.

Mark Hays

Review Title: The flight was excellent but they charged 15% tipping on full price without authorisation
Review Text:
So I bought 4 Groupons at $75 for our family (a total of $300) when we visited Miami in June 2012. The booking process was very easy. They answered the phone promptly, had our Groupon codes down and sent us a boarding pass for 2 flights as we split into two parties as we take turn to look after a young baby. They told us that tax and gratuity were not included and if we want to pay by credit card we should call one day before or we will need to pay by cash to the pilot. I called the day before our flights and said I want to pay the tax by credit card and will give the pilot tip in cash. Knowing Floridan tax is about 7% that would be roughly $20 so I didn't ask them to confirm the total amount charged.
The flight was very enjoyable. The pilot has a lot of local knowledge and was very pleasant. He told us that he owns this company and two planes and he is going to buy a new bigger plane.
My husband said that the pilot shouldn't expect any tip as he would make a lot of money from this business. However, I decided to tip him because I enjoyed his talk about the area.
We received an invoice of $110 in my email stating "GT for flights". I called them up to clarify. The same lady who took my credit card confirmed the tax was $20 and the rest was for gratuity I said I only authorised the tax charge and I already tipped the pilot and that I never authorised them to do that on my credit card. She told me I need to talk to Tony. The first thing he asked me "How much did you tip the pilot?" When I told him, he said bluntly "That is not customary. It should be 15% on the full price of the flights which is $600 if you didn't buy from Groupon". Thats why they charged me $90. He asked or "offered" me if I want to get a refund of $40 for the tip that I already gave the pilot.
I believe in tipping but it is for service people who earn $8.50/ hour at restaurants/ hotels who rely on tipping for their living. However, for a pilot who earns a high wage or owns his own company, tipping should be at customer's discretion, not by forced tipping which is the case here.
What I also found that their attitude was defiant about the charge when it was clear that I did't authorise it. What was not transparent was they didn't itemise the tax charge of $20 in my $110 invoice but indicated it all as GT for gratuity.
I wondered if they did that to avoid the tax and try to capture the discount they offered on Groupon. I have written to them to request the full refund. I hope to hear from other people's experiences.

Review Title: Fun way to see the skyline of Miami from the sky
Review Text:
Normally, the only way you get to see Miami from the sky is by watching the opening sequence of an old episode of Miami Vice or the new (now-canceled) Charlie's Angels. Miami Seaplane Tours is a nice alternative. It's a bit pricey, but if you check carefully, you might find a Groupon for half-off (like I did). The plane seats 3 passengers maximum, so don't plan on doing this in a large group.
The pilot was about 15 minutes late for our scheduled departure, but he did give us the full half-hour flight that we paid for. We flew over Downtown Miami, the man-made islands in Biscayne Bay, and South Beach. The pilot pointed out some of the multi-million dollar homes owned by famous people and some of the other well-known landmarks. Unfortunately, the mikes are only one-way (you can hear the pilot, but you can't talk to him), so we couldn't ask any questions. The pilot also played a soundtrack of current pop hits to fill the gaps when he wasn't narrating.

Here are some tips:
Most taxi drivers will have no clue where this place is, so you have to tell them to go west on Rickenbacker Causeway and turn left at the road for the Rickenbacker Fish Company (and make a QUICK LEFT onto the dirt road just before you get to the Rickenbacker Fish Company).
Wear flipflops or Tevas, because you may have to wade through ankle-deep water to board the plane.
The Rickenbacker Fish Company is a decent restaurant a short walk from the Miami Seaplane Tours dock. It opens for lunch at noon. I had the blackened mahi mahi sandwich and fries, which were very tasty. The Rusty Pelican restaurant is a bit farther away, and it was closed for renovation when we were there.
The staff at the Rickenbacker Fish Company are very friendly and will call you a taxi while you're finishing your meal (you won't have much luck flagging one down on the causeway).
Go with the half-hour seaplane tour. One hour would probably get a bit boring.
If you use a Groupon, be sure to call for reservations and bring the confirmation number with you (either as a printout or on your cell phone).
